title.en: EU reaches agreement to simplify AI rules, responding to industry compliance complaints
title.zhHans: 欧盟达成简化 AI 规则协议，回应行业合规负担诉求

searchSummary.en: EU agreed to simplify AI rules in 2026, responding to industry compliance burden complaints. How the world’s first AI regulation evolved to balance innovation and safety.
searchSummary.zhHans: 欧盟 2026 年达成简化 AI 规则协议，回应行业对合规负担的诉求。世界上第一部 AI 监管法规如何演变以平衡创新与安全。

summary.en: On May 7, 2026, the European Council and European Parliament reached a provisional agreement to streamline the EU AI Act's requirements, responding to widespread industry feedback that the original rules were overly complex and burdensome. The agreement modified key provisions related to high-risk classification, documentation requirements, and small-entity exemptions, aiming to make the world's first comprehensive AI regulation more workable while maintaining its core safety objectives.
summary.zhHans: 2026 年 5 月 7 日，欧洲理事会和欧洲议会就简化欧盟 AI 法案的要求达成临时协议，回应了广泛的行业反馈——原始规则过于复杂和繁重。该协议修改了与高风险分类、文档要求和小型实体豁免相关的关键条款，旨在使全球第一部综合性 AI 监管更可行，同时保持其核心安全目标。

narrative.en: The EU AI Act had been celebrated as a historic achievement when it passed in 2024, but its implementation revealed practical challenges. Companies reported that the risk classification system was difficult to apply to rapidly evolving AI capabilities. Documentation requirements were onerous, especially for smaller developers. The definition of 'high-risk' systems captured too many low-risk applications. The simplification agreement, reached on May 7, 2026, addressed these concerns through several key changes: clarifying the criteria for high-risk classification to exclude low-risk applications; reducing documentation requirements for SMEs and open-source developers; extending transition periods for certain compliance obligations; and clarifying rules for general-purpose AI models. The agreement demonstrated the EU's willingness to adapt its regulatory approach based on real-world implementation experience. It was seen as a mature response to the tension between the need for AI safety regulation and the practical challenges of implementing such regulation at scale. The simplification was generally welcomed by industry, though safety advocates expressed concern that it weakened protections. The agreement was a reminder that AI regulation was not a one-time legislative act but an ongoing process of refinement.
narrative.zhHans: 欧盟 AI 法案在 2024 年通过时被誉为历史性成就，但其实施揭示了实际挑战。公司报告说，风险分类系统难以适用于快速演变的 AI 能力。文档要求过于繁重，特别是对较小的开发者。"高风险"系统的定义捕获了太多低风险应用。2026 年 5 月 7 日达成的简化协议通过几项关键修改解决了这些问题：澄清高风险分类标准以排除低风险应用；减少中小企业和开源开发者的文档要求；延长某些合规义务的过渡期；以及澄清通用 AI 模型的规则。该协议展示了欧盟根据实际实施经验调整其监管方法的意愿。它被视为对 AI 安全监管需求与大规模实施此类监管的实际挑战之间紧张关系的成熟回应。业界普遍欢迎简化，尽管安全倡导者对削弱保护表示担忧。该协议提醒人们，AI 监管不是一次性的立法行为，而是一个持续的完善过程。

description.en: First major revision of the world's first AI regulation. Demonstrated regulatory adaptability to real-world implementation feedback. Set precedent that AI regulation would evolve based on experience, not remain static.
description.zhHans: 全球第一部 AI 监管的首次重大修订。展示了监管对实际实施反馈的适应性。开创了 AI 监管将基于经验演变而非保持静态的先例。

text.en: The European Council and European Parliament reached a provisional agreement on May 7, 2026 to streamline EU AI Act requirements.
text.zhHans: 欧洲理事会和欧洲议会于 2026 年 5 月 7 日就简化欧盟 AI 法案要求达成临时协议。
